Who should Bangladesh be trading with?. [ dhakatribune ]
item.description:
The first answer is that we've got to stop thinking of it being a “country” that trades. The people within a country, yes. Organizations of companies inside it, yes. But the country itself doesn't trade.
Maybe when the government buys aircraft or something. But nearly all trade is between people and organizations that just happen to be inside some lines on the map, not a country doing something.
Therefore, because it's just people doing their own thing, it's not really for us to determine how much of it is done. It's all up to them -- the buyers and sellers.
But we can still go further than this.
Recent statistics show that China is the major trading partner of Bangladesh (21% of total trade) and then India and the US each about 8.5% -- India slightly ahead. The question we might want to ask ourselves is, well, is that about right?
The standard theory of trade revolves around the “gravity model.” This works just like gravity and the planets -- bigger and closer has more effect than smaller and further away.
So, the standard guide is that an economy will trade more with a larger economy and also more with one that is closer.
So, a large economy that's close to us - China - should be a major trading partner. This seems obvious enough.
The US is a long way away but it's also a very large economy so that seems fine.
India is a very much smaller economy than either of those two yet it's right next door. That too seems fine.
Which is about as far as most applications of this gravity model get. We should note that when people really calculate this, we find that the gravity model really does work. This really does explain global trade numbers.
Except -- we do not mean mere geographical position when we talk about distance here. We mean, instead, economic distance.
This is influenced by geography, yes, but isn't quite the same thing. What we really mean here is: “How difficult is it to do the trade over this distance?” So, transport links matter.
In medieval Europe, for example, it was the sea and rivers that were the easy transport routes. So there could be -- and often was -- more trade between coastal Spain and coastal Italy than there was between the coast and 100 miles inland in either country.
The roads were so bad, compared to water transport, that the economic distance over 500 miles on water could be shorter than that over 50 miles on land.
We can also add in things like language as a barrier to trade, or whether the kings are at war. In this modern world, we also have to think about laws -- tariffs, customs posts, differences in standards that block trade.
It's this last part that we can change. Which is the thing that really makes this concept of economic distance different from geographic distance. We can change economic distance by just changing our own barriers to trade.
Do note that this is an area of economics where there's no right answer. Not one that we can point to and say: “This number should be this.” But once we translate the gravity model to the correct concept of economic - not just geographic - distance, Bangladesh probably doesn't trade enough with India.
Yes, it's a smaller economy than China and the US, but it is also right next door. If that's true -- I would say it is even as others could argue that I'm wrong -- then one of the easy ways to make Bangladesh richer is simply to make it easier to trade with India.
Sort out the land ports, make it easier and faster to clear goods through customs, lower the tariffs, and so on. But then I think Bangladesh should do that anyway, so it's not exactly a difficult conclusion for me to reach.
Tim Worstall is senior fellow at Adam Smith Institute in London.

item.title: Why does the heat persist even though its rains every day?
item.description:
Zahur Hossain wiped the sweat from his brow as he stood at the Farmgate metro station waiting for his train to Motijheel. Despite the short distance from his home, he took a rickshaw to get there. Even that short journey left him drenched in sweat.

"The moment I step outside, I start sweating. It''s raining, but there''s no sign of the heat letting up," he said.

Many people in Dhaka share Zahur''s experience. But it is not only those out on the streets who are suffering. People staying indoors, whether cooking, doing household chores or carrying out other daily activities, are also struggling with the oppressive heat.

For the past few days, Dhaka and much of Bangladesh have seen an erratic alternating of sun and clouds. Intermittent rain fell on Sunday morning, leaving the sky overcast by 11:00 am. Yet, instead of bringing relief, the rain has only intensified the muggy, uncomfortable atmosphere.

Rain would normally bring relief from the heat. Meteorologists, however, say several factors are preventing that from happening. These include latent heat released after rainfall, excessive moisture in the air, the monsoon not yet in full swing and the continued inflow of humid air from the south.

Muhammad Abul Kalam Mallik, a senior meteorologist at the Bangladesh Meteorological Department, told Prothom Alo that even after rainfall, the Earth''s surface is not cooling quickly. Instead, heat stored in the ground and urban concrete structures builds up again after the rain.
As a result, latent heat is released into the atmosphere, making the environment feel warmer.

He added that the amount of water vapour currently present in the air is unusually high. This prevents sweat from evaporating easily from the human body, making temperatures feel hotter than they actually are.

The clouds that form during the monsoon season are generally located close to the Earth's surface. Rain from these clouds does not provide immediate relief. Mallik said prolonged rainfall would bring greater comfort but such continuous rain has yet to occur.

While the monsoon entered Bangladesh about a week later than usual this month and has now spread across the country, it remains weak.
Meteorologist Kazi Zebunnesa said the monsoon has expanded nationwide but has not yet become fully active. As a result, the country is not experiencing sustained and sufficient rainfall.

At the same time, large volumes of humid air are entering Bangladesh from the south and across the Bay of Bengal. This is increasing the amount of moisture in the atmosphere and contributing significantly to the muggy conditions.

She added that a western low-pressure area currently persists over the southwestern region near the Sundarbans. As a result, humidity levels remain particularly high there, making conditions feel even more uncomfortable.

Meteorologists say much of the rain currently falling across the country is brief and scattered. Rainwater therefore evaporates quickly and returns to the atmosphere, further increasing humidity. At the same time, the lack of widespread, long-lasting rainfall means environmental temperatures are not dropping significantly.

According to weather experts, meaningful relief is likely only if the monsoon becomes more active and brings moderate to heavy rainfall across most parts of the country for several consecutive days. Until then, the alternating pattern of sunshine and rain is expected to keep the humid heat in place.

The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has already forecast that rainfall during this year's monsoon season may be below normal, while temperatures could remain higher than usual.

On Saturday, the country's highest temperature was recorded in Ishwardi, Pabna, at 36.7 degrees Celsius.

item.title: The FY2026-27 digital agenda. [ dhakatribune ]
item.description:
[Priority]

Systemic Significance

Selected by: Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen-3-32B, GPT-OSS-120B, GPT-OSS-20

The national budget for FY 2026-27 signals a bold and aggressive policy shift aimed at completely transforming the digital ecosystem of Bangladesh. Officially elevating the information and communication technology sector into its top 10 strategic national priorities, the government has laid down a monumental challenge to expand the combined technology and telecommunications footprint from its current 1-2% to a staggering 10% of the nation's total gross domestic product within the next five years. To fund this ambitious leap into a high-tech future, the newly announced financial plan allocates Tk2,049 crore to the Information and Communication Technology Division and an additional Tk2,141 crore to the Posts and Telecommunications Division. These major resource allocations are tightly bound to wide-ranging structural tax and tariff adjustments designed to stimulate rapid market growth, though a comprehensive reading of the proposals reveals a complicated dual landscape of immense industry opportunities mixed with serious operational obstacles. For the domestic software arena and individual digital workers, this budget acts as an unprecedented financial springboard. The government has introduced a sharp reduction in advance tax from 5% down to 2%, coupled with a total withdrawal of import duties and value-added tax on fully built-up technology hardware components like laptops, desktop computers, enterprise servers, printers, flash memory, and high-resolution monitors. This dramatic regulatory rollback provides instant operational cost relief to established software companies expanding their physical tech architectures. At the same time, it significantly lowers the high economic entry barrier that previously restricted students, aspiring freelancers, and small boutique IT firms from accessing high-performance computational devices, thus instantly boosting the baseline capacity of the national technology workforce. The entrepreneurial ecosystem receives an equally vital lifeline through newly structured tax-free statuses and widespread value-added tax exemptions tailored for startups, digital content creators, and independent freelancers. This legislative support is further reinforced by a dedicated Tk500cr early-stage Startup Fund, which carries a strict state mandate to prioritize financing for youth and women-led digital commerce platforms and software collectives. Alongside these individual incentives, the macro digital economy is set to experience a surge in local enterprise demand via a massive structural push for digital public infrastructure (DPI), anchored by the launch of a unified national identity and digital wallet initiative. Building and managing these secure identity pipelines will create multi-year development projects for local system integrators and cybersecurity firms, while the seamless payment flow will bypass historical monetization bottlenecks for mobile application developers and e-commerce merchants alike. The telecommunications sector, which has historically operated under a punishing cumulative tax burden approaching 57%, finally receives some relief in this budget proposal. The withholding tax on standard mobile network services has been trimmed down from 12% to 10%. Far more significantly, the 20% withholding tax previously levied on revenue sharing, statutory license fees, and other ongoing regulatory charges payable to the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission has been completely dismantled. This systemic change liberates massive pools of working capital for telecom operators, allowing them to redirect resources toward expanding the essential 4-G and 5-G networks required to carry the intense data loads generated by the government's smart state initiatives. Furthermore, to protect the long-term goal of making Bangladesh a regional hub for technology exports, the administration has extended critical tax benefits for local mobile manufacturing plants until June 2030. This extension locks in lower advance income taxes of just 1% on 22 essential raw manufacturing materials, providing international investors with multi-year policy predictability. Despite this array of business-friendly incentives, the budget simultaneously introduces complex friction points and unintended negative consequences that could slow the country's digital trajectory if left unmanaged. While dropping import barriers on fully assembled laptops and servers is fantastic for technology users, it places domestic hardware assemblers at an immediate and devastating disadvantage. Local manufacturers operating within high-tech parks lose their protective competitive tariff cushions, leaving them vulnerable to cheaper, mass-produced global imports that can now flood the open market completely duty-free. A similar policy contradiction emerges in the consumer telecom sector. The outright abolition of the flat Tk300 SIM card tax is a highly progressive move intended to lower the initial connectivity barrier for low-income and rural subscribers. However, this relief is instantly counterbalanced by the introduction of a 15% VAT on the base supply price of all physical SIM cards and e-SIMs, meaning the onboarding cost for premium digital transitions will remain highly sticky. This shift also creates an immediate fiscal challenge, as removing the traditional SIM tax will drop state revenue by an estimated Tk1,200cr in the coming fiscal year. In an economy struggling to stabilize a massive project deficit, this steep decline will undoubtedly put pressure on the National Board of Revenue to enforce highly aggressive auditing measures or impose tighter compliance scrutiny across other flourishing segments of the local IT ecosystem. Finally, the budget reveals a disconnect between high-level digital policy goals and physical infrastructure realities. The state's aggressive vision for an AI-driven economy relies heavily on high-density GPU server rooms and advanced local cloud systems. Yet, these next-generation data centres require tremendous, uninterrupted electrical power. Because the budget proposal fails to include direct, heavy subsidies for green energy integration or guaranteed continuous heavy power grids for designated IT parks, local operators will face exorbitant running costs from backup generator systems, which threatens to completely wipe out the financial advantages gained from the duty-free import of enterprise servers. Similarly, the capital-intensive push toward microelectronics and semiconductor architecture is left exposed, as the budget lacks the direct cash-back incentives or specialized equity funds needed to attract physical wafer fabrication plants to the region. Ultimately, while the budget successfully transforms the tech sector from a simple tax target into an engine of growth, its ultimate success will depend entirely on how effectively the state addresses these underlying physical power, security, and local manufacturing challenges when implementation begins on July 1. Syed Almas Kabir is former President, BASIS and Chairman, Bangladesh ICT & Innovation Network (BIIN).

item.title: BSF gathers 125 people for ‘push-in’ at Darshana border, BGB on alert
item.description:
India’s Border Security Force (BSF) has allegedly attempted to push 11 men and women across the Darshana–Joynagar border in Chuadanga.

The attempt was made near border pillar 77 S-2 at around 4:00 am on Sunday. However, members of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) thwarted the move, forcing the BSF to withdraw the group to another location.

Meanwhile, BGB has received information that a further 125 people have been assembled on the Indian side of the border. Officials assume there may be attempts to push them into Bangladesh.

Confirming the incident, Lieutenant Colonel Md Nazmul Hasan, commanding officer and director of the Chuadanga Battalion (6 BGB), said the BSF had attempted to push 11 Bengali-speaking men and women across the border. The effort failed as BGB personnel intervened, and the individuals were subsequently removed from the area by the BSF.

“According to the latest information available to us, the BSF has moved the 11 individuals from the Darshana–Joynagar border area to the opposite side of Baradi–Sultanpur,” he said. “Through our own sources, we have learned that another 125 people have been gathered near the border and may be subjected to a similar push-in attempt. BGB remains on high alert in the area.”

This is the first reported attempt by the BSF to carry out a push-in operation along this particular stretch of the border in recent months. Following similar incidents elsewhere along the frontier, patrols have been intensified throughout the area under the jurisdiction of 6 BGB.

Local residents have also been advised to remain vigilant amid concerns over further attempts to push people across the border.

item.title: State minister: Govt introduces major reform in primary teacher transfer process
item.description:
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj on Sunday said the government has introduced a new decentralized system for teacher transfers to make the process transparent, accountable, and free from corruption.
The teacher transfer process had long been known as a major area of syndicate control and corruption, which stood as a significant obstacle to improving the quality of education, he said while addressing the Validation Workshop on the Bangladesh Education Sector Analysis (ESA) 2026, organized by GPE and UNICEF at a hotel in the Dhaka.
Bobby Hajjaj said that under the directive of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and the initiative of the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education, the teacher transfer process has been decentralised and brought to the local level.
Under the new policy, separate committees are being formed at the upazila, district, divisional, and city corporation levels to review transfer applications at regular intervals, he said.
At the upazila level, a four-member committee headed by the Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) will scrutinize applications, while the Upazila Primary Education Officer will issue transfer orders based on the committee’s recommendations, he added.
Besides, similar five- or six-member committees will operate at the district, divisional, and city corporation levels to examine transfer applications and issue transfer orders, he said.
Education and Primary and Mass Education Minister Dr A N M Ehsanul Hoque Milon attended the program as the chief guest.
Officials from the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education, relevant departments, and UNICEF were also present at the event.

item.title: এবার একসঙ্গে ১২৫ জনকে সীমান্তে জড়ো করেছে বিএসএফ, প্রস্তুত বিজিবিও
item.description:
ভারতীয় সীমান্তরক্ষী বাহিনী (বিএসএফ) চুয়াডাঙ্গার দর্শনা-জয়নগর সীমান্ত দিয়ে ১১ নারী-পুরুষকে পুশইনের চেষ্টা চালিয়েছে। রবিবার (১৪ জুন) ভোর ৪টার দিকে সীমান্তের ৭৭ এস-২ পিলারের পাশ দিয়ে এ চেষ্টা চালানো হয়। তবে বর্ডার গার্ড বাংলাদেশের (বিজিবি) প্রতিরোধের মুখে বিএসএফ তাদের অন্যত্র সরিয়ে নেয়।
এদিকে দুপুরে আরও ১২৫ জনকে সীমান্ত এলাকায় জড়ো করা হয়েছে বলে তথ্য পেয়েছে বিজিবি। তাদের পুশইন করা চেষ্টা করা হবে বলে আশঙ্কা সংশ্লিষ্টদের।
চুয়াডাঙ্গা ব্যাটালিয়নের (৬ বিজিবি) পরিচালক ও অধিনায়ক লেফটেন্যান্ট কর্নেল নাজমুল হাসান ঘটনার সত্যতা নিশ্চিত করেছেন। তিনি জানান, বিএসএফ ১১ জন বাংলাভাষী নারী-পুরুষকে পুশইনের চেষ্টা চালায়। বিজিবি সদস্যদের প্রতিরোধের মুখে তারা ব্যর্থ হয় এবং ওই ব্যক্তিদের সরিয়ে নেয়।
বিজিবির এই কর্মকর্তা বলেন, ‘সর্বশেষ পাওয়া তথ্য অনুযায়ী বিএসএফ ওই ১১ জনকে দর্শনা-জয়নগর সীমান্ত থেকে বারাদী-সুলতানপুরের বিপরীতে নিয়ে গেছে। নিজস্ব সূত্রে জানতে পেরেছি দুপুরে আরও ১২৫ জনকে পুশইনের জন্য সীমান্তের বিপরীতে জড়ো করে রাখা হয়েছে। নিয়ন্ত্রিত এলাকায় বিজিবির কঠোর অবস্থানে আছে।’
সাম্প্রতিক সময়ে এই সীমান্তে বিএসএফের এটিই প্রথম পুশইনের চেষ্টা। বিভিন্ন সীমান্তে পুশইনের চেষ্টার ঘটনার পর ৬ বিজিবি নিয়ন্ত্রিত এলাকায় টহল জোরদার করা হয়েছে। স্থানীয় বাসিন্দাদেরও সতর্ক থাকতে বলা হয়েছে।

item.title: ভারতের আপত্তিতে নেপালের অতিরিক্ত বিদ্যুৎ পাচ্ছে না বাংলাদেশ
item.description:
সঞ্চালন লাইনের সক্ষমতার অজুহাত দেখিয়ে ভারতের আপত্তিতে আটকে গেছে বাংলাদেশে নেপালের অতিরিক্ত ২০ মেগাওয়াট বিদ্যুৎ রফতানির পরিকল্পনা। ফলে আগামীকাল ১৫ জুন থেকে বাংলাদেশে কেবল পূর্বনির্ধারিত ৪০ মেগাওয়াট বিদ্যুৎ রফতানি করবে নেপাল। সংশ্লিষ্ট জ্বালানি কর্মকর্তাদের বরাতে এ তথ্য জানা গেছে। নেপালের সংবাদমাধ্যম কাঠমান্ডু পোষ্ট এ খবর জানিয়েছে।
কর্মকর্তারা জানিয়েছেন, ভারতের সেন্ট্রাল ইলেকট্রিসিটি অথরিটি (সিইএ) সঞ্চালন লাইনের সক্ষমতার সীমাবদ্ধতার কারণ দেখিয়ে এই অতিরিক্ত ২০ মেগাওয়াট বিদ্যুৎ রফতানির অনুমোদন স্থগিত করেছে। এর ফলে নতুন করে একটি সংশোধিত বা নতুন ত্রিপক্ষীয় চুক্তি এবং নেপাল-ভারত জ্বালানি সচিব পর্যায়ের যৌথ স্টিয়ারিং কমিটির (জেএসসি) সিদ্ধান্তের মতো আরও কিছু প্রক্রিয়ার প্রয়োজনীয়তা দেখা দিয়েছে।
২০২৫ সালের ২৭ নভেম্বর ঢাকায় অনুষ্ঠিত জেএসসি বৈঠকে বিদ্যমান ৪০ মেগাওয়াটের পাশাপাশি আরও ২০ মেগাওয়াট বিদ্যুৎ রফতানি বাড়াতে নীতিগত সম্মতি হয়েছিল। সেই অনুযায়ী নেপাল ইলেকট্রিসিটি অথরিটি (এনইএ) ভারতের এনটিপিসি বিদ্যুৎ ব্যবসা নিগম লিমিটেডকে (এনভিভিএন) এই অতিরিক্ত ২০ মেগাওয়াট রফতানির সুবিধা দিতে আনুষ্ঠানিকভাবে অনুরোধ জানায়। কিন্তু এনভিভিএন পরে জানায় যে, ভারত-বাংলাদেশ ১,০০০ মেগাওয়াট সক্ষমতার সঞ্চালন লাইনটি এই অতিরিক্ত বিদ্যুৎ পরিবহনে সক্ষম নয়।
এনইএর বিদ্যুৎ বাণিজ্য বিভাগের পরিচালক থার্কা বাহাদুর থাপা বলেন, এবার বাংলাদেশে কেবল ৪০ মেগাওয়াট বিদ্যুৎ রফতানি হবে। অতিরিক্ত ২০ মেগাওয়াটের জন্য ত্রিপক্ষীয় চুক্তি এখনও সম্পন্ন হয়নি। তবে আগের ৪০ মেগাওয়াটের ব্যবস্থার মতোই আমরা এনভিভিএনের মাধ্যমে ভারতের সিইএর কাছে প্রক্রিয়া শুরু করেছিলাম। কিন্তু তারা জানিয়েছে, সঞ্চালন লাইনে অতিরিক্ত ২০ মেগাওয়াটের সক্ষমতা নেই।
কর্মকর্তারা জানিয়েছেন, প্রস্তাবিত এই সম্প্রসারণের জন্য এখন নেপালে অনুষ্ঠেয় নেপাল-ভারত জেএসসি এবং সচিব পর্যায়ের যৌথ ওয়ার্কিং গ্রুপের (জেডব্লিউজি) বৈঠকে সিদ্ধান্ত প্রয়োজন হবে। তবে এসব বৈঠকের সময়সূচি এখনও নির্ধারণ করা হয়নি।
এর আগে ২০২৪ সালের ৫ জানুয়ারি নেপাল-ভারত জেএসসি বৈঠকে ভারতের সঞ্চালন ব্যবস্থা ব্যবহার করে বাংলাদেশে ৪০ মেগাওয়াট বিদ্যুৎ রফতানির বিষয়ে নীতিগত সমঝোতা হয়। সেই অনুযায়ী এনইএ, এনভিভিএন এবং বাংলাদেশ বিদ্যুৎ উন্নয়ন বোর্ডের (বিপিডিবি) মধ্যে ত্রিপক্ষীয় চুক্তির ভিত্তিতে রফতানির ব্যবস্থা করা হয়।
পরে ২০২৪ সালের ২ অক্টোবর নেপাল ও বাংলাদেশের মধ্যে আরেকটি জেএসসি বৈঠকে ত্রিপক্ষীয় চুক্তির বিষয়ে অগ্রসর হওয়ার সিদ্ধান্ত হয়। পরদিন এনইএ, বিপিডিবি ও এনভিভিএনের মধ্যে চুক্তি সই হয়। এর আওতায় প্রতি বছর ১৫ জুন থেকে ১৫ নভেম্বর পর্যন্ত বাংলাদেশে ৪০ মেগাওয়াট বিদ্যুৎ রফতানি করা হচ্ছে।
এনইএ জানিয়েছে, অতিরিক্ত ২০ মেগাওয়াট বিদ্যুৎ রফতানির জন্য নেপাল-ভারত জেএসসিতে আলোচনা, ভারতের সিইএর অনুমোদন এবং নতুন ত্রিপক্ষীয় চুক্তি প্রয়োজন হবে। অনুমোদন মিললে বাংলাদেশে মোট রফতানি ৬০ মেগাওয়াটে উন্নীত হবে, তবে অন্যান্য শর্ত অপরিবর্তিত থাকবে।
নেপাল প্রথমবারের মতো ২০২৪ সালের ১৫ নভেম্বর ১২ ঘণ্টার জন্য বাংলাদেশে বিদ্যুৎ রফতানি করে। দেশটির বিদ্যুৎ প্রথমে ধালকেবার-মুজাফফরপুর ৪০০ কেভি সঞ্চালন লাইনের মাধ্যমে ভারতে প্রবেশ করে। পরে বহরমপুর-ভেড়ামারা ৪০০ কেভি লাইনের মাধ্যমে বাংলাদেশে আসে।
